artist.name: S1gns Of L1fe
artist.tagline: Ambient composer, sound designer and co-founder of Synphaera Records
roles: Co-founder of Synphaera, Exosphere, Material, Assemblage & Aura
One half of Ascendant (with Don Tyler)
Solo projects: S1gns Of L1fe and Starterra
Host of the Harmonic Horizons podcast
Music director, SomaFM's Synphaera Radio (with Don Tyler)
artist.shortBio: Chris Bryant is an ambient composer and sound designer based in the Pacific Northwest who records as S1gns Of L1fe and Starterra, is one half of Ascendant, and co-founded Synphaera Records. A lifelong guitarist who taught for almost 19 years, he has devoted himself to ambient music since 2012, and today he teaches it to a global community and builds his own instruments.
longBio: Chris Bryant grew up in the San Francisco Bay Area and now calls the Pacific Northwest home. At nine he bought his first heavy metal tape, Iron Maiden's Seventh Son of a Seventh Son, and when "Moonchild" came through his sister's silver boombox his life changed. He formed his first band at 11 or 12 and played in bands all through high school, while a friend down the hall kept playing The Orb and The Future Sound of London, music that seemed almost alien to him.

A road trip through Idaho's Sawtooth Mountains, with Dave Matthews and Tim Reynolds playing acoustic guitars on the stereo, sent him on a long guitar quest. He made his living as a guitar teacher for almost 19 years, running his own studio and helping students go on to schools like Berklee, USC and NYU.

In 2012 a chance conversation about the music of Solar Fields hit like a lightning bolt. With a computer and a copy of Reason he started from zero, and within months his track Metamorphosis was drawing encouragement on KVR and SoundCloud. He called the project S1gns Of L1fe, with two 1s for Highway 101, the road that carves up California to the redwoods, and for the ones and zeros of binary code. His debut, Language of The Ancients, followed in 2013.

Grammy-nominated mastering engineer Don Tyler heard the music and reached out, and their first five songs together became Ascendant's New Land EP in 2014. When the label they most wanted to join turned down their album, they started their own. Synphaera Records, its name borrowed with Klaus Schulze's blessing, grew into a family: the cinematic Exosphere, the Material sound design wing, the community label Assemblage and Aura, their monthly subscription portal on Bandcamp. His music has aired on Hearts of Space, Echoes, SomaFM and Star's End.

When the world locked down in 2020, Chris called it his make-or-break moment. He committed to truly learning sound design, building every patch from scratch, and he made his first Starterra album, Celestial. Both paid off: Material became a home for his soundsets, and Starterra became his most experimental voice. His solo albums, from Pathways to Ascension to Portal to Transcendence (2024), explore vibration, consciousness and the cosmos.

For the first 11 years of his ambient career he still taught guitar full time to support his family. In 2023 he finally stepped away to put everything into music, his labels, YouTube, his Patreon community, one-to-one coaching and, more recently, his own plugins. He believes the strongest intuitive voice is often the quietest, that energy is the real currency of human work, and that the best way to keep music alive is to support artists directly.

timeline.title: Moonchild, then ambient
timeline.detail: At nine, Chris buys his first metal tape, Iron Maiden's Seventh Son of a Seventh Son. He plays in bands from age 11 through high school, while a friend introduces him to The Orb and The Future Sound of London.

timeline.title: A life in guitar
timeline.detail: A drive through Idaho's Sawtooth Mountains with Dave Matthews and Tim Reynolds on the stereo starts a long guitar quest. Chris makes his living as a guitar teacher.

timeline.title: Chris Bryant Guitar School opens
timeline.detail: Chris runs a guitar school in Los Gatos, California, part of a guitar-teaching career that lasts almost 19 years.

timeline.title: The lightning bolt
timeline.detail: A conversation about Solar Fields changes everything. Within months his first track, Metamorphosis, is drawing encouragement on KVR and SoundCloud. He names the project S1gns Of L1fe, for Highway 101 and binary code, and meets Don Tyler.

timeline.title: Debut album: Language of The Ancients
timeline.detail: The first S1gns Of L1fe album comes out on January 23, 2013. It is inspired by biology, astronomy and the harmony of existence.

timeline.title: Branches in the Sky
timeline.detail: A 40-minute, five-track follow-up EP recorded in spring 2013. It is his debut on Spain's Arecibo Records.

timeline.title: Building Ambient Online
timeline.detail: Chris runs the ambientonline.org forum and hosts the Ambient Online Podcast. He is credited as producer on Ambient Online Compilation Vol. 1.

timeline.title: Ascendant is born
timeline.detail: After hearing S1gns Of L1fe, Don Tyler reaches out. Their first five songs become Ascendant's debut EP, New Land (February), followed by Source Transmission in April.

timeline.title: Ascendant in Helsinki
timeline.detail: Ascendant travels from California to appear at the Ambient Music Conference in Helsinki, Finland (June 27–28).

timeline.title: A "no" that started a label
timeline.detail: After waiting two and a half months, the best-known label in the genre passes on Ascendant's album. Chris and Don decide to do it themselves.

timeline.title: Hearts of Space: Ethersphere
timeline.detail: Program 1040 (April 4, 2014) is his first Hearts of Space feature, with three S1gns Of L1fe tracks. Ascendant follows that summer on Midsummer Night 3; by 2026 the show has featured his music in 24 programs.

timeline.title: Synphaera Records launches
timeline.detail: After a label they admired turned them down, Chris and Don start their own. Synphaera launches with Ascendant's Æthereal Code (SYN01) on July 21, 2015.

timeline.title: Meridian and Starseed
timeline.detail: Ascendant's Meridian (June 2016) trades beat-driven anthems for sequenced, drifting ambient. That August the label's first various-artists compilation, Starseed, arrives.

timeline.title: Producing live on Twitch
timeline.detail: Chris streams ambient and downtempo production sessions in Ableton Live on Twitch every weekday morning.

timeline.title: Pathways to Ascension
timeline.detail: His first solo album on Synphaera (January 24, 2017) is built on the idea that everything in the universe is vibration.

timeline.title: The idea for Exosphere
timeline.detail: While walking through San Francisco waiting to perform at a street festival, Don pitches a darker, cinematic imprint. Chris agrees on the spot.

timeline.title: The Source Trilogy concludes
timeline.detail: Ascendant's Particle Horizon (November 7, 2017) completes the trilogy begun with Source Transmission and Æthereal Code.

timeline.title: Exosphere launches
timeline.detail: Synphaera's imprint for dark ambient, drone and deep cinematic space music releases its first titles.

timeline.title: The S1gns Of L1fe hub goes live
timeline.detail: Chris launches s1gnsofl1fe.com with a rebrand, a blog, services, coaching bookings and merch.

timeline.title: The make-or-break year
timeline.detail: In lockdown, Chris commits to mastering sound design and makes his first Starterra album, Celestial (October 20, Exosphere). Material by Synphaera starts releasing soundsets.

timeline.title: The Age of Cymatics
timeline.detail: S1gns Of L1fe returns on January 26, 2021. Weeks later Star's End plays "Dimensional Shift".

timeline.title: All in on YouTube
timeline.detail: Chris commits to his YouTube channel and a Patreon community that gets a new post every other day.

timeline.title: Hearts of Space: Wintertronic 3
timeline.detail: Program 1332 (December 9, 2022) features "Astral Plane" from Pathways to Ascension.

timeline.title: Going all in
timeline.detail: After almost 19 years teaching guitar, including 11 years alongside his ambient career, Chris steps away to focus on music, his labels, coaching and YouTube.

timeline.title: Hearts of Space: Star Tracer
timeline.detail: Program 1340 (March 17, 2023) features the title track of The Age of Cymatics.

timeline.title: Aura opens
timeline.detail: Chris and Don launch Aura, an exclusive subscription portal for archival, remastered and new music from Ascendant, S1gns Of L1fe, Starterra and more.

timeline.title: Made in Ableton Live
timeline.detail: Ableton features Chris building "Particle Acceleration" from a single sample in its Made in Ableton Live video series (February 2024).

timeline.title: Astral Ascendant and Starfall
timeline.detail: Ascendant releases two companion albums. Cyclical Dreams Magazine later names Starfall its album of the year for 2024.

timeline.title: Portal to Transcendence
timeline.detail: His third solo album on Synphaera arrives on May 21, 2024. It is his first since starting his YouTube channel and Patreon community.

timeline.title: Schallwelle Preis recognition
timeline.detail: At Germany's Schallwelle awards, Portal to Transcendence ties for 2nd place for Ambient Album. Ascendant and Starterra also place in the Ambient Album category.

timeline.title: Two weeks in Japan
timeline.detail: A long-held dream. His field recordings become the free Sounds of Japan pack.

timeline.title: Performance Series begins
timeline.detail: Chris starts an ongoing series of recorded live performances across S1gns Of L1fe and Starterra.

timeline.title: Black Ocean in Wuppertal
timeline.detail: In March 2025, Chris and Martin Stürtzer record a 35-minute space ambient live set on Martin's hardware synths in Germany.

timeline.title: Memory of Light
timeline.detail: The Starterra album is ranked #70 in Cyclical Dreams Magazine's 200 Best Albums of 2025.

timeline.title: Instrument maker
timeline.detail: Chris releases a growing set of his own instruments. They include the free Texture Loom (June), the Stellarizer MIDI sequencer (July) and the TRANQUILITY synthesizer.

timeline.title: Regenesis
timeline.detail: Ascendant's new album (June 2, 2026) continues the shift toward Berlin School sequencing and hardware and modular production.

stories.title: Two Ones: The Name S1gns Of L1fe
stories.subtitle: Highway 101, binary code and a new beginning
body: Why the 1s? When Chris chose the name in 2012, he swapped the i's in Signs and Life for ones. Read them together and you get 101.
In California, 101 is a highway. It carves its way up the state, along the coast to the redwood forests, home to some of the largest and oldest trees in the world.
101 is also the language of machines: the ones and zeros of binary code, the digital world where his music is born.

"That name really stuck with me and I just gravitated towards it," he says. "That's when S1gns Of L1fe was born." A road through ancient forests and a line of code. It is a fitting name for music that joins the natural and the electronic.

stories.title: Moonchild: From Metal to Guitar Teacher
stories.subtitle: The road that led to ambient
body: Chris was nine when he bought his first heavy metal tape: Iron Maiden's Seventh Son of a Seventh Son. His sister, a Grateful Dead and Bob Marley fan, looked at it and asked if he was sure. He was. She put it in their silver boombox, the opening track "Moonchild" began, and his life changed.

He formed his first band at 11 or 12 and played in bands all through high school. On days when he wasn't at metal shows, a friend was always playing The Orb and The Future Sound of London. Chris couldn't imagine how that music was even made. It sounded alien, and it stayed with him.

Then, on a drive through Idaho's Sawtooth Mountains, a friend put on Dave Matthews and Tim Reynolds playing acoustic guitars together. "I've never heard music like that before," he remembers. It sent him on a guitar quest that became a career.

For almost 19 years Chris made his living teaching guitar, eventually from his own studio in the Bay Area. Some of his students went on to Berklee, USC and NYU. Even after ambient music took over his life in 2012, he kept teaching full time to support his family, until 2023, when he stepped away to go all in.

sources.name: ChatterBlock: Chris Bryant Guitar School, Los Gatos

stories.title: The Lightning Bolt
stories.subtitle: 2012: the conversation that changed everything
body: By 2012 Chris felt he was waiting for something, "waiting for divine inspiration," as he puts it. He had tried producing upbeat electronic music in the early 2000s and let it go, but the idea never left the back of his mind.

Then, in a random conversation, a friend asked whether he had heard the music of Solar Fields. That was the moment. "All of a sudden I knew what I had to do," he says. He stopped everything and walked a new path.

He started with just a computer, a license for Reason and an old copy of Digital Performer. The first experiments were, in his words, really awful. But the learning came fast, and within two or three months he posted a track called Metamorphosis on KVR and SoundCloud. The response was encouraging: "I might have something here."

SoundCloud in 2011 to 2013 was a real social network for music: free, ad-free and full of producers lifting each other up. Chris shared every track but one from his debut there before it came out. Language of The Ancients was released in January 2013.

stories.title: First Signals
stories.subtitle: Language of The Ancients and the Ambient Online years
body: The first S1gns Of L1fe album, Language of The Ancients, came out in January 2013 after almost every track had already been shared on SoundCloud. Chris wrote that it was inspired by biology, astronomy and the quiet harmony running through all existence.
Months later came Branches in the Sky, a 40-minute EP recorded in spring 2013. It continued the story and marked his debut on Arecibo Records, a young ambient label in Spain.

Chris was also building community. He ran the Ambient Online forum and hosted the Ambient Online Podcast, which showcased members' drones and soundscapes. Its long-running compilation series helped keep the site alive.
Even then, the signature was clear: hypnotic drones, pulsing rhythms and a fascination with where we come from.

stories.title: Two Worlds Collide: Ascendant
stories.subtitle: A friendship built over Dropbox
body: Don Tyler heard S1gns Of L1fe and sent Chris a message: he was a producer in Los Angeles with some tracks lying around, and maybe they could collaborate. Don turned out to be a Grammy-nominated mastering engineer with a deep love of synthesis. Chris had never collaborated before, but he said yes. Their first five songs became Ascendant's New Land EP in 2014.

The name has meaning. Your ascendant is the zodiac sign rising in the east when you are born: the face you show the world and the lens you see it through. Ascendant also has a deep lore of worlds and stories, with every album placed on a timeline. Astral Ascendant and Starfall (2024) go back before New Land.

The two have met in person only three or four times. For more than a decade they have passed sessions back and forth across the West Coast. When Don settled on Logic Pro, Chris learned it too, so they could finally share the same sessions. When Don heard the first Astral Ascendant sketch he wrote back that it was "the stuff that the gods forged."

Their styles clash, in the right way. "When those two things come together," Chris says, "magic happens." Radio agreed early on: Hearts of Space, Echoes, SomaFM and Star's End have all played Ascendant.

sources.name: Ambient Visions: AV Talks with Chris Bryant and Don Tyler

stories.title: Collaboration in the Sky
stories.subtitle: How a "no" became Synphaera Records
body: In 2014 Chris and Don submitted an album to the best-known label in their genre. They waited two and a half months. The answer came back kind but final: it broke the label's heart, but they couldn't take it. "We were crushed," Chris says.

So they decided to do it their way, which meant doing it themselves. They knew the pitfalls going in and went in unafraid of the work. Synphaera Records launched in 2015 with Ascendant's Æthereal Code.

The name comes from Klaus Schulze's 1973 double album Cyborg, where the word appears with an umlaut. "Syn" means together and "phaera" means atmosphere, so they read it as "collaboration in the sky", perfect for music about space and air. They asked Schulze's office for permission. He said yes, on one condition: spell it correctly. No umlaut, because it wouldn't translate on the web. Use "ae".

The family grew from there: Exosphere for deep cinematic space music, Material for sound design, Assemblage as a community label, and Aura for exclusive monthly releases. The standard never changed. Chris sees a label as "the last front line" before the uncurated noise, so listeners can trust a record before they even press play.

sources.name: Ambient Visions: AV Talks with Chris Bryant and Don Tyler

stories.title: A Solar System of Labels
stories.subtitle: Exosphere, Material, Aura and beyond
body: In 2017, walking the streets of San Francisco while waiting to perform at a street festival, Don pitched a new imprint to Chris. He already had a name: Exosphere. Chris loved it instantly.

The spark was an album by Martin Stürtzer that was too dark for Synphaera. Don couldn't stop listening to it. Exosphere launched in 2018 as a home for drone, dark ambient and deep cinematic space music.
Chris maps the labels onto the solar system. Synphaera is the core sound, the inner planets from the Sun to Mars, while Exosphere lives beyond the asteroid belt, where light meets darkness.

The family kept growing: Material in 2020 for soundsets and production tools, Aura as an exclusive portal to their own music, and newer imprints for modular music (Assemblage) and community releases (Pénte).

sources.name: Ambient Visions: AV Talks with Chris Bryant and Don Tyler

stories.title: 2020: The Make-or-Break Year
stories.subtitle: Sound design, Starterra and the birth of Material
body: When the world locked down in 2020, everyone turned inward. Chris asked himself what he really wanted to do. "This is my make-or-break moment," he decided, and he made two commitments.

The first was to truly become a sound designer. He had always shaped sounds, but he wanted the real language of synthesis. So he forced himself to build every patch from scratch, dissect other people's patches, read the books and ask friends for help.
The second was a record. Exosphere had existed for a couple of years, but Chris had never made an album for it. That became Celestial, the first Starterra album, released in October 2020.

Both paid off for years to come. The sound design grew into Material, the Synphaera family's sound design wing, where he has released soundsets and preset packs. The same skills now power his tutorials, his mentorship and the instruments he builds.

stories.title: Three Projects, Three Lenses
stories.subtitle: How Chris keeps Ascendant, S1gns Of L1fe and Starterra distinct
body: Chris juggles a lot: three main projects, labels, YouTube, Patreon and a podcast. The way he keeps his music distinct is by treating each project as its own mindset and method.
Ascendant has a fixed palette. He works with a specific set of synths and tools, the ones he knows give results, and limits himself to them, because that is what Ascendant is.
With S1gns Of L1fe he widens the aperture. More tools and more colors are allowed, but it still has to sound like S1gns Of L1fe.

Starterra is where he lets it all go. At a slow 70 to 75 BPM, sounds can come from anywhere. It is his most experimental project, and just as important to him, even if some S1gns Of L1fe listeners haven't found it yet.

stories.title: An Album Made With Its Listeners
stories.subtitle: Portal to Transcendence and twelve years around the cosmos
body: Chris posts something on Patreon every other day: videos, presets, packs and starter tracks, often built live across multi-part series. Over time a big folder of those pieces grew.
When he senses a S1gns Of L1fe album coming, it's a profound moment. "This is my front-facing identity," he says. So he went through the folder and picked the best of the best.

Because many of those songs had been made live in front of his community, the album felt interactive. "People had helped me make this album," he says. All that energy flowed into one nexus point, which became the name of one of the tracks.

Listening to the final mix of Portal to Transcendence next to one of his early albums, the difference was night and day. Twelve years is one full cycle of the Chinese zodiac, dragon to dragon. "It's been quite the trip around the cosmos."

stories.title: Ikigai: Recording Japan
stories.subtitle: Two weeks, a field recorder and an open heart
body: Japan had been a lifelong dream for Chris. Before he ever went, he felt a strong pull toward it, and his wife is half Japanese, so the trip also meant family roots. They spent about two weeks there. "I think everybody who goes there leaves changed," he says.

What stayed with him most was the people. Train staff, taxi drivers and hotel workers were kind and took real pride in their work. He connected it to ikigai, the Japanese idea of purpose and a way of living, and found it deeply inspiring.
He went with a field recorder, his iPhone and an open mind, to capture the essence of the place, from futuristic Tokyo to quieter moments in between.
Those recordings became The Sounds of Japan, a free field recording pack you'll find in the Bonus Vault.

stories.title: Meridian: Leaving the Beat Behind
stories.subtitle: The album that changed Ascendant, and a studio that keeps evolving
body: Ascendant's first two albums were full of beat-driven anthems. With Meridian (2016), they replaced much of that with heavily sequenced, drifting ambient. It was new territory, and the album wasn't easy to make.
Fans welcomed the change. For Chris, that response was the moment he knew the vision behind Synphaera could go far beyond one project.

The duo's tools changed over time too. Ascendant began entirely in software, and by the 2024 twin albums Astral Ascendant and Starfall they were about half hardware. Today they work almost entirely in hardware and modular.
The process begins with story. Tracks often start as emails about Ascendant's deep lore. Then comes sound design, and arrangement and mixing come last.

sources.name: Ambient Visions: AV Talks with Chris Bryant and Don Tyler

stories.title: Everything Is Vibration
stories.subtitle: The ideas behind the solo albums
body: Chris's solo albums read like chapters of one cosmic story. Pathways to Ascension (2017) begins from the idea that everything in the universe is vibration, and that we are all rising toward a higher frequency.
The Age of Cymatics (2021) takes its name from the study of how sound shapes matter. Its tracks imagine sound waves awakening genetic memory and drawing listeners into one shared consciousness.
Portal to Transcendence (2024) is the next step: passing through the portal into a new age. It invites the listener into a world where time and space dissolve.

For Chris, space music is about both outer space and the imagined space within. Astrology and the cycles of the solar system are a steady source of direction, and many listeners use the music for meditation, focus and spiritual practice.

sources.name: Ambient Visions: AV Talks with Chris Bryant and Don Tyler

stories.title: Tapping Into the Void
stories.subtitle: Intuition, flow and the quietest voice
body: Chris believes every artist knows "the void", the endless well that all creativity comes from. It is free and always open, day or night.

He is intuitive by nature, and he does his best work when he is uninhibited and flowing, not worrying what anyone thinks. When he stops to overthink, he stumbles. "The intuitive voice that's the strongest," he says, "is often the quietest." You have to listen hard for that first voice.

He tunes in through meditation, exercise and treating his body right, along with practical habits: set goals and track them, and learn your tools until they disappear. One exercise he suggests is to loop a single element, sit with it for a minute, and ask your intuition what comes next.
Underneath it all is a belief that music is a universal language, and that what we create from a heart-centered place ripples out to everyone around us.

stories.title: Energy Is the Real Currency
stories.subtitle: Aura, Bandcamp and the value of human-made music
body: Chris and Don started Aura as an exclusive, subscription-based label on Bandcamp. Subscribers get each new monthly release and everything before it: unreleased Ascendant, Starterra, Remote Vision, Phase47 and more. None of it is on streaming services.

It's a response to how music was devalued. A stream might pay an artist a tiny fraction of a cent, so independent artists need millions of plays just to pay the bills. On Bandcamp, most of a $10 album goes straight to the artist.

For Chris it comes down to energy. "Our real currency on this planet is energy," he says. Money is just how we exchange it. When someone puts hours of their human energy into a piece of music, that work has value that an AI-generated track can't replace.
His advice for listeners is simple: support the artists you love directly. "That's the only way."

stories.title: Teaching the World to Make Ambient
stories.subtitle: From Twitch streams to one of YouTube's go-to ambient channels
body: Chris has always taught. For almost 19 years it was guitar, and he loved watching students graduate and go on to Berklee, USC and NYU. In 2016 he was already streaming ambient production live on Twitch.

Around 2021 he went all in on YouTube. His channel became one of the platform's go-to places for ambient production, with more than 490 videos, over 4 million views and more than 44,000 subscribers. On Patreon he posts every other day: videos, presets, packs and multi-part track builds. He also hosts his own podcast, Harmonic Horizons.

What he finds most rewarding is seeing students reach their goals. Many don't want to go pro. They just want to reach a standard they're proud of. "When I see them release their first track," he says, "that's the most satisfying thing."
In 2023 he stepped away from guitar teaching to focus on it all. Today he offers one-to-one coaching, a six-week mentorship, and Ambient Music Production for Beginners, his coaching app on Studio.

stories.title: One Sample, a Whole World
stories.subtitle: Inside Chris's Made in Ableton Live episode
body: In February 2024, Ableton invited Chris into its Made in Ableton Live video series. The result was "Particle Acceleration", a track built entirely from ideas sparked by a single sample.
He layers glitchy percussion, ethereal pads and intertwining melodies. He also uses Chance tools, LFOs and Beat Repeat to add controlled randomness, so the track keeps shifting without falling apart.
Plucked tones are turned into evolving washes of sound with Granulator, and the episode closes with his tips on melody, arrangement and mixing.
The finished track came out on Synphaera, and the session template he uses is available through Material as Utility.

sources.name: Ableton Blog: Made in Ableton Live

stories.title: Building the Tools He Needed
stories.subtitle: Presets, plugins and instruments born in the studio
body: Chris sees plugins as sculpting tools. He has called them his "chisels", tools for stretching a sound without breaking it.

For years he shaped other people's instruments, making videos, presets and soundbanks for companies like Ableton, Steinberg, Output, Baby Audio, Lunacy Audio and Audiomodern. Through Material he released preset libraries such as Ancient Technology, Eternia, Chromatic and Anomaly.

Then he started building his own. SOL, a free reverb made with Dawesome, came first. The free Texture Loom, the Stellarizer MIDI sequencer, Glitchwork, Parallax Well and the TRANQUILITY synthesizer followed.
Each one begins with a musical need. With TRANQUILITY, he wanted a synthesizer that stays alive after the patch is built.

stories.title: Down the Eurorack Rabbit Hole
stories.subtitle: Modular synthesis as a path of discovery
body: Chris's Eurorack journey began with simple curiosity and soon became an obsession. Every patch revealed new sounds and possibilities.

His rack is built around exploration: Make Noise MATHS and TEMPI for modulation and time, Instruō arbhar and Qu-Bit Stardust for granular and tape textures, and an OXI One sequencer to tie it together.
For him, modular is a way of discovering himself as much as sound. It taught him to embrace imperfection, stay curious and follow the music wherever it leads.
That path now shapes his records. Ascendant has moved almost entirely to hardware and modular, and Synphaera's Assemblage imprint is devoted to music made through live patching and deep listening.

sources.name: Ambient Visions: AV Talks with Chris Bryant and Don Tyler

stories.title: Live, From California to Wuppertal
stories.subtitle: Performing ambient music on stage and on camera
body: Chris has performed for audiences around the world. In 2014, Ascendant traveled from California to the Ambient Music Conference in Helsinki. In 2017, the duo played a street festival in San Francisco.
At Ascendant shows, people have even danced, a reminder that Synphaera's core sound carries a real pulse.
Chris shares what he has learned about performing ambient music in tutorials. In 2025 he started the Performance Series, recorded live sets under both S1gns Of L1fe and Starterra.

In March 2025 he visited Martin Stürtzer's studio in Wuppertal, Germany. Together they recorded Black Ocean, a 35-minute space ambient set played live on Martin's hardware synths. The only soft synth was a pad from Chris's own Hive soundset.

sources.name: Ambient Visions: AV Talks with Chris Bryant and Don Tyler

stories.title: On the Airwaves
stories.subtitle: Radio, awards and a channel of their own
body: Radio has been part of the story from the start. Ascendant's early releases were played by SomaFM, DI.FM, Hearts of Space, Star's End and Echoes, and those plays helped convince Chris and Don to build a label.

Hearts of Space has featured his music in 24 programs since 2014, 36 broadcasts counting repeats: 12 as Ascendant, 7 as Starterra and 5 as S1gns Of L1fe, from "Ethersphere" (2014) to "Stellaris" (2026). Star's End has also played his music, including "Dimensional Shift" and "Alchemy of the Infinite".
SomaFM gave the label its own station, Synphaera Radio, with Chris and Don as music directors.
In 2024, Portal to Transcendence tied for second place for Ambient Album at Germany's Schallwelle awards, and Cyclical Dreams Magazine named Ascendant's Starfall its album of the year.

I wanted a synthesizer that stayed alive after the patch was built.
Embrace imperfection, stay curious, and follow the music wherever it leads.
This album draws inspiration from the natural and social complexities of our environment.
"Space Music" to us reflects not only physical space, but the imaginary space within.

quotes.text: People are craving authenticity, especially in music.

source.name: Ambient Visions: AV Talks with Chris Bryant and Don Tyler

interviews.title: Five questions for Synphaera Records
interviews.summary: Chris and Don Tyler explain why they launched Synphaera in 2015, how early radio support for Ascendant shaped them, and how they got Klaus Schulze's blessing for the name. They also describe their quality-first release policy.

interviews.title: V/A :: Starseed (Synphaera)
interviews.summary: A review of Synphaera's first various-artists compilation, compiled by Chris and Don and opened by Ascendant's "Inception". The reviewer ranks it among the strongest ambient/downtempo compilations in years.

interviews.title: Ascendant: Æthereal Code (review)
interviews.summary: A detailed track-by-track review of Ascendant's second album and Synphaera's first release. It places the album between new age, space ambient and psytrance.

interviews.title: S1gns Of L1fe: The Age of Cymatics
interviews.summary: A short review praising the album's vibrant, well-produced cosmic electronics and its emotional drive across eight tracks.

interviews.title: Made in Ableton Live: S1gns Of L1fe
interviews.summary: Chris builds "Particle Acceleration" from a single sample, using Chance tools, LFOs and Beat Repeat for controlled randomness and Granulator for evolving textures. He closes with tips on arrangement and mixing.

interviews.title: S1gns Of L1fe: Portal to Transcendence
interviews.summary: A review welcoming the first S1gns Of L1fe album in three years, describing its seven sequencer-driven tracks as detailed, spacious and almost blissful.

interviews.title: Chris Bryant: S1gns of 1nf1n1ty
interviews.summary: A wide-ranging conversation with host Marius-Christian Burcea: the meaning behind the name S1gns Of L1fe, growing up on heavy metal, almost 19 years of teaching guitar, the 2012 moment that changed everything, founding Synphaera with Klaus Schulze's blessing, Starterra's lockdown birth, Aura, and why energy is the real currency of music.

interviews.title: Black Ocean: liveset and album with S1gns Of L1fe
interviews.summary: Martin Stürtzer describes Chris's visit to his Wuppertal studio and the 35-minute space ambient set they recorded live on his hardware synths.

interviews.title: Martin Stürtzer & S1gns of L1fe: Black Ocean
interviews.summary: A review of the Wuppertal collaboration. It notes the set was a first take after the two programmed the sounds and planned the structure together.

interviews.title: A Conversation with Chris Bryant (S1gns Of L1fe, Starterra, Ascendant)
interviews.summary: A conversation of nearly two hours, made for Brückner's 100th video. It covers Chris's projects, his philosophy as a curator and label owner, AI, spirituality in music and heavy metal.

interviews.title: S1gns of L1fe Shares his Top Five Plugins for Ambient Music
interviews.summary: Chris picks Dawesome KONTRAST, Excite Audio Motion: Fractal, Arturia Pigments 6, Lunacy Audio BEAM 2.0 and FabFilter Pro-R 2, and explains how each shapes depth and motion in his ambient work.

interviews.title: Synphaera: AV Talks with Chris Bryant and Don Tyler
interviews.summary: An in-depth interview covering Ascendant's origins, the rejection that led to Synphaera, the birth of Exosphere, how the labels work with artists, and the duo's move to hardware and modular. Chris also talks about authenticity in the age of AI.

interviews.title: S1gns Of L1fe releases FREE Texture Loom atmosphere engine plugin
interviews.summary: News coverage of the free dual-sample atmosphere engine, which turns simple source material into evolving pads, drones and textures.

interviews.title: S1gns Of L1fe Releases Texture Loom - Free Dual-Sample Atmosphere Engine
interviews.summary: KVR's news item announcing Texture Loom in VST3, AU and Max for Live formats. A follow-up covers the v1.1 update.

interviews.title: S1gns of L1fe introduces Stellarizer performance-to-pattern MIDI sequencer
interviews.summary: A news story on Stellarizer, which records a live MIDI performance, analyzes its timing, contour and velocity, and generates related patterns across Near, Far and Deep Space ranges.

interviews.title: Hearts of Space PGM 1332: Wintertronic 3
interviews.summary: A program on sequencer-driven electronic music that includes "Astral Plane" from Pathways to Ascension.

interviews.title: Hearts of Space PGM 1340: Star Tracer
interviews.summary: A program on modern synth and plugin-driven space music that includes the title track of The Age of Cymatics.

interviews.title: Star's End playlist 02.14.21
interviews.summary: Host Chuck van Zyl opens the show with "Dimensional Shift" from The Age of Cymatics.

interviews.title: Star's End playlist 06.02.24
interviews.summary: Host Chuck van Zyl opens the show with "Alchemy of the Infinite" from Portal to Transcendence.

interviews.title: Synphaera Radio
interviews.summary: A dedicated, commercial-free SomaFM channel for the Synphaera catalog, programmed with Chris and Don as music directors.

interviews.title: The Ambient Music Conference, Helsinki
interviews.summary: Event post referencing a performance by Ascendant traveling from California.

labels.name: Synphaera Records
labels.description: An independent label for modern electronic ambient and space music. It launched with Ascendant's Æthereal Code, and its name comes from a Klaus Schulze track, used with his blessing.

labels.name: Exosphere
labels.description: Synphaera's imprint for dark ambient, drone, atmospheric soundscapes and deep cinematic space music. It is home to Starterra.

labels.name: Material by Synphaera
labels.description: Soundsets, presets, templates and production tools for license-free use. It includes Chris's Ancient Technology, Eternia, Chromatic and Anomaly libraries and the Utility template for Ableton Live.

labels.name: Aura
labels.description: An exclusive, subscription-based label on Bandcamp with new releases every month: unreleased Ascendant, Starterra, Phase47 and more, available nowhere else.

labels.name: Assemblage
labels.description: Synphaera's imprint for modular and systems-based electronic music shaped through live patching and deep listening.

labels.name: Pénte
labels.description: Synphaera's community imprint for themed compilations, collaborative editions and discovery-focused releases.

labels.name: Arecibo Records
labels.description: A Spanish ambient label that released S1gns Of L1fe's Branches in the Sky EP in 2013.

vault.subtitle: A full ambient track, start to finish
vault.summary: Chris builds a complete ambient track from the first sound to the final arrangement, using a range of synthesizers and techniques to help take your music to the next level.
body: Want to follow along with the exact modular setup from the video? Grab the free VCV Rack patch below, open it in VCV Rack (free) and explore it as you watch.

vault.title: Ambient Drone Starter Pack
vault.subtitle: Five 24-bit drones from the modular
vault.summary: Five drone samples recorded in 24-bit from Chris's modular synthesizer, made to go with the “Ambient drones for beginners” tutorial.
body: In the companion video, Chris builds a deep, atmospheric drone step by step using nothing but a free sample, the free Vital synth and a mix of free and paid effects. Download the pack, then build your first drone alongside him.

vault.title: Particle Glow Sample Pack
vault.subtitle: For the Absolute Beginners tutorial
vault.summary: The ambient sample pack from “Ambient Tutorial for Absolute Beginners”, with four extra bonus samples.
body: In the tutorial, Chris makes an ambient track from scratch with a few very simple tools and techniques: sampling, Vital for the bass, and a sequence. Perfect if you're opening a DAW for the first time.

vault.title: Nexus Peak Preset & MIDI Pack
vault.subtitle: Rebuild a track from Portal to Transcendence
vault.summary: The Vital presets and MIDI files behind “Nexus Peak”, so you can recreate the track yourself.
body: “Nexus Peak” is from the S1gns Of L1fe album Portal to Transcendence on Synphaera. In the companion video Chris walks through how to rebuild it: load the presets, drop in the MIDI and follow along.

vault.title: Beginner Ambient Tutorial
vault.subtitle: A 30-minute track with free Vital presets
vault.summary: Create an ambient track from scratch in Vital, using a free pack of presets Chris designed for this lesson.
body: S1gns Beginner Pack 02 has eight Vital presets: a bass, a sequence, three pads, a soundscape, a lead and a sweet ambient pluck. Download it below and build the track with him.

vault.title: Creating Icy Drones From Scratch
vault.subtitle: Four ways to conjure cold, otherworldly drones
vault.summary: Those dark, icy drones that conjure alien landscapes aren't about owning the right gear. It's how you use the tools you already have.
body: **FM is your friend.** Frequency modulation pushes shimmering upper harmonics into your reverb and sounds fantastic in the low registers. No dedicated FM synth? Vital and Serum can do “pseudo FM” between oscillators. Tame it with an envelope or LFO, because things get wild fast. Surge XT, Dune 3 and Phase Plant are great here too.

**Embrace modular.** Modular gives you true FM in many flavours and total control over what modulates what. VCV Rack (free), Voltage Modular, Softube Modular or real Eurorack all work. Keep experimenting with synthesis and modulation; you can even run audio into modulation inputs.

**Reverb for space.** Don't just max out size and decay and let the reverb do everything. Keep size and decay high, but start with the mix around 25–50%. The drone's natural harmonics come through, and the reverb carries on where the synth leaves off.
**Don't forget the bass.** A slow-moving bass layer gives your drone a foundation the listener can feel. Pair it with an icy pad drone and the effect is far more dramatic than either on its own.

vault.title: The Sounds of Japan
vault.subtitle: Free field recordings
vault.summary: A free collection of field recordings from Japan: raw material for textures, beds and atmospheres.
body: Recorded on a two-week trip that fulfilled a lifelong dream. Chris took a field recorder and his iPhone to capture the spirit of Japan, from futuristic Tokyo to its quieter corners.

vault.title: 16 Free Glitch Percs
vault.subtitle: Hits, clicks and textures
vault.summary: Glitch percussion hits, clicks and textures for ambient, IDM and experimental beats. Instant futuristic rhythm for your tracks.

vault.title: Texture Loom 1.5
vault.subtitle: A free dual-source granular instrument
vault.summary: Load two samples and weave them into evolving pads, drones, cinematic beds and playable clouds. For macOS (AU/VST3) and Windows (VST3).
body: Each source can play back conventionally or as a cloud of grains, with control over grain size, density, spray, stereo width and pitch jitter.
Eight-voice polyphony, two Motion generators and a modulation matrix with up to 16 routes keep your textures moving.
Two multimode filters, an equal-power blend between the sources and a built-in reverb shape the space. An updated 26-page manual is included.

vault.title: SOL
vault.subtitle: A free reverb made with Dawesome
vault.summary: A free reverb built around light, space and motion, created by S1gns Of L1fe with Dawesome. For Mac and Windows.
body: SOL blends ambient space, granular glitter and tonal shimmer in one fast, intuitive interface.

GLITTER adds a granular layer and CALM smooths it. SHINE adds pitched grains an octave or two up, CLOUDS sets the size and density of the reverb, SPACE sets depth and stereo spread, and COLOR makes the wet sound darker or brighter.
Want more? Solara, Ascendant's companion pack of 20 presets for SOL, is on Material.
